swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests 2>&1 | tail -1 || true
description:
**A `ph://` job is never staged on iOS, so the one source this library says it must copy is the one it doesn't.** `SourceResolver.stageIfRequired` (`ios/Sources/Amphora/Core/SourceResolver.swift:62`) has ZERO callers — `grep -rn stageIfRequired ios/` returns only its definition. Its Kotlin twin is called at `android/src/main/kotlin/dev/amphora/core/DefaultUploadEngine.kt:217`, inside `prepare()`, before `SourceResolved` is dispatched and before the remote resource is created. The Swift engine instead dispatches `.sourceResolved(... stagedPath: current.stagedPath)` with a path nothing ever set, and both Swift transports then build the body as `URL(fileURLWithPath: job.stagedPath ?? job.sourceUri)` — a file URL whose path is the literal string `ph://...`. Tasklist `900` recorded this as a live defect and deliberately kept the callee (docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md §2.3; dead-code-removal.md §3: 'the caller is missing, not the callee'). This tasklist supplies the caller.

**Why it is more than one missing line.** `PHAsset` is the ONE iOS source that genuinely cannot be seeked: the documented exception to 'no chunk temp files', and the only place on iOS where a storage reservation comes into play (ROADMAP §3; Phase 4 ranks 'iOS / Photos asset' third among the device rows). Until this lands, a device run of that row would be exercising a bug.

**Why the vectors never noticed.** They are a pure-function suite over `reduce` plus three I6 transport observations (conformance-vectors.md §3.4). No row reaches either engine's preparation step, so a port that forgets to stage stays green. The fix is therefore two things: the call itself, and a shared row that goes red when a port drops it, proven by a negative control on both ports.

**A second defect, read from source while authoring and NOT executed — US-3 confirms or refutes it by running it red first.** Kotlin's `prepare()` reads `sources.stageIfRequired(job, storage) ?: if (job.sourceKind == SourceKind.CONTENT_URI && job.stagedPath == null) { dispatch(job.id, UploadEvent.SpaceDenied(job.sizeBytes)); return null } else null`. `stageIfRequired` returns `null` for a SEEKABLE `content://` (`open(job).use { null }`), so a seekable provider — the case `70` built to stream with zero copies — appears to be sent to `BLOCKED(STORAGE_LOW)` every time. A genuine reservation refusal already arrives as `StorageReservationDenied`, which `runSlice` maps to `SpaceDenied` by itself. The shared negative row in US-3 is designed to catch exactly this.

**Depends on `140`**, so that the Swift half of the new vector and control runs in the `ios` CI job rather than only on one developer's machine.

**Scope guard.** No real Photos library, no device, and no simulator result substituted for either. The staging rows prove OUR call order and bookkeeping. They do not prove `PHAssetResourceManager` export behaviour, iCloud-offloaded originals, or `StorageManager.allocateBytes` under real pressure — those stay `NOT YET VERIFIED — physical device`.

userStories.title: Photos sits behind a seam, so a ph:// job can be exercised without a Photos library
acceptanceCriteria: Every Photos touchpoint on the `ph://` path goes through one injected `Sendable` abstraction: the `PHAsset.fetchAssets` lookup and size / `modificationDate` read in `SourceResolver.probe` (which `enqueue` and `isIntact` both reach), and the `PHAssetResourceManager` write in `StorageGovernor.exportPhotosAsset`. The default implementation is today's PHAsset-backed code, moved rather than rewritten. `AmphoraUploader.configure`'s public signature is unchanged, so a host sees no difference.

The export still writes to the reservation URL `StorageGovernor` hands out — `Application Support/Amphora/Staging/<jobId>.part`, excluded from backup — never `Caches` or `tmp`. The seam is TOLD its destination and cannot choose one. That placement is the direct fix for the origin bug, and a seam that let a test double pick its own path would stop proving it.
`ios/Package.swift` still declares zero external dependencies, and no XCTest or mocking library is introduced (CLAUDE.md §4 explains the executable-target harness).

GATES: `swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` exit 0; `swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests` exit 0 with its summary line quoted; `.chief/verify.sh` exit 0 (with `Gradle build` SKIPPED named, not green).
userStories.notes: swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors: exit 0, warnings clean. swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests: exit 0 — "Amphora path tests: 46 passed (4 upload-path cases, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors)" (count unchanged; US-2 adds the behaviour case). chief verify: exit 0, "verify: 5 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed" with the skip named — "Gradle build — no JDK on PATH" — so Android is UNVERIFIED locally, not green. New seam: ios/Sources/Amphora/Core/PhotosAssetSource.swift — protocol PhotosAssetSource (metadata(forLocalIdentifier:) throws -> PhotosAssetMetadata; export(localIdentifier:to:) async throws -> Void) plus SystemPhotosAssetSource, the moved PHAsset code. export returns Void and is TOLD its destination, so no implementation can pick a path: StorageGovernor still passes reservation.url (Application Support/Amphora/Staging/<jobId>.part, excluded from backup) and still returns it. Injected via SourceResolver(storage:photos:) and StorageGovernor(capacityProvider:photos:), both defaulting to SystemPhotosAssetSource(); AmphoraUploader.configure signature untouched (grep: no call-site changes needed). PhotosAssetSource.swift is now the only file importing Photos — SourceResolver.swift and StorageGovernor.swift no longer do. One deliberate merge, not a pure move: the two former size readers disagreed (SourceResolver.estimatedSize scanned every resource for an Int64 fileSize; StorageGovernor.resourceSize read only the first resource but also accepted NSNumber) — the seam accepts either representation from any resource, a superset of both. ios/Package.swift untouched: zero external dependencies, no XCTest, no mocking library.

userStories.title: The Swift engine stages where Kotlin does, and a ph:// job reaches the transport as a staged file
acceptanceCriteria: Red first: write the behaviour test below against the UNFIXED engine, record how it fails (the message), then fix. A test first seen green could be testing nothing.

`DefaultUploadEngine.startTransfer`'s create-on-first-run branch calls `sources.stageIfRequired(current)` BEFORE dispatching `.sourceResolved` and BEFORE `transport.create`, and passes the returned path as `.sourceResolved(... stagedPath:)` — the order of `prepare()` in `DefaultUploadEngine.kt`. The reducer already persists the path and flips `sourceKind` to `.stagedCopy` (`UploadStateMachine.swift` ~lines 45-51); do not duplicate that in the engine ('the machine decides, the engine acts').

A refused reservation — `TransportError.remainderStagingDenied` from `stageIfRequired`, `StorageError.stagingDenied` from the export — dispatches `.spaceDenied(needed:)` and never calls `create`. That is the Swift twin of Kotlin's `StorageReservationDenied -> SpaceDenied` in `runSlice`. Other staging failures follow Kotlin's handling at the same point; name the mapping in notes.

Behaviour test in `ios/Tests/AmphoraTests/UploadPathTests.swift`, counted in `pathCases`, with an injected Photos double serving known bytes. Enqueue `ph://<id>` and assert: the recorded order puts the export before `create` (export, then create, then head, then an append at offset 0 — one shared call log across the Photos double and `RecordingTransport`); the row's `stagedPath` is non-nil, lies inside `StorageGovernor.stagingDirectory()`, and holds exactly the double's bytes; `sourceKind == .stagedCopy`; and the transport's `startTransfer` was handed that job. A second assertion covers refusal: with a capacity provider that cannot fit the asset, the job is `BLOCKED(STORAGE_LOW)`, `create` is never called, and no `.part` file is left behind.

The negative stays negative: `plainFileUploadRunsCreateAppendCompleteInOrder` still records exactly the three calls it records today (create, head, an append at offset 0), with no staging call. A plain file costs zero extra storage (I6), and a fix that staged everything would pass the Photos test and fail this one.
`pathCases` and the Swift summary count change. Update every place that quotes `46` (grep — do not guess; CLAUDE.md §4 is one), with a dated correction wherever a doc's claim changed.

GATES: `swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` exit 0; `swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests` exit 0 with its new summary line quoted; `Tests/Conformance/drift-control.sh --port swift` exit 0; `.chief/verify.sh` exit 0 (with `Gradle build` SKIPPED named, not green).
userStories.notes: Red first, then green. Against the UNFIXED engine the new case trapped with `AmphoraPathTests/UploadPathTests.swift:78: Precondition failed: wire calls were ["create", "head", "append:0"]` — no `export`, because `stageIfRequired` had no caller. Fix: `DefaultUploadEngine.startTransfer`'s create-on-first-run branch now calls `sources.stageIfRequired(current)` before `.sourceResolved` and before `transport.create`, and passes `staged?.path` as `.sourceResolved(stagedPath:)` — the order of Kotlin's `prepare()`. The reducer still owns persisting the path and flipping `sourceKind` to `.stagedCopy`; the engine adds no policy. Error mapping, matching Kotlin's `runSlice` around `prepare()`: `TransportError.remainderStagingDenied(needed)` -> `.spaceDenied(needed:)` and `StorageError.stagingDenied` -> `.spaceDenied(needed: current.sizeBytes)` (that case carries no payload; Kotlin's `StorageReservationDenied.requestedBytes` is the same quantity), both returning before `create`; every OTHER staging failure falls through to the existing `.transportError(classify(error))` catch, which is Kotlin's `catch (error: Exception)` at the same point. New case `photosAssetIsStagedBeforeTheRemoteIsCreated`, counted in `pathCases` (4 -> 5): one shared `CallLog` actor across `FakePhotosAssetSource` and `RecordingTransport` recorded `["export", "create", "head", "append:0"]`; the row's `stagedPath` was non-nil, prefixed by `StorageGovernor.stagingDirectory()`, and held exactly the double's 24 bytes; `sourceKind == .stagedCopy`; `transport.transferredJob` was that job id with that `stagedPath`. Refusal half (capacityProvider `{ 0 }`): call log EMPTY (create never reached), state `.blocked` with `blockReason == .storageLow`, and no `<jobId>.part` left behind. The negative stayed negative — `plainFileUploadRunsCreateAppendCompleteInOrder` still asserts exactly `["create", "head", "append:0"]` with no staging call, and passes. GATES OBSERVED: `swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` exit 0; `swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests` exit 0 — "Amphora path tests: 47 passed (5 upload-path cases, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors)"; `Tests/Conformance/drift-control.sh --port swift` exit 0 — "drift-control: 2 control(s) ran, 0 skipped, 0 failure(s)"; `chief verify` exit 0 — "verify: 4 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed" with the skip named, "Gradle build — no JDK on PATH — UNVERIFIED, not passed", so Android is unverified locally, not green. Count updates: grepped `46 passed` / `4 upload-path` across the tree — CLAUDE.md §4's two current claims updated to 47 / 5 with a dated correction added to CLAUDE.md's Corrections section. The other seven files quote what run `34675666580` printed or what a past tasklist observed; a run's log does not change, so those were deliberately left alone and the correction says so.

userStories.title: One staging section in the shared fixture, run by both ports through the engine's own preparation step
acceptanceCriteria: `Tests/Conformance/vectors.json` gains a staging section (for example `sourceStaging`) with three rows, each carrying a `spec` that points at state-machine.md / persistence-and-recovery.md §3. `stage-01-unseekable-source`: a source that cannot be seeked (iOS: a `ph://` Photos asset; Android: a `content://` provider whose descriptor is not seekable) is copied under a reservation of `sizeBytes` BEFORE the remote is created, and `SourceResolved` carries a non-null `stagedPath` whose bytes equal the source's. `stage-02-seekable-source-not-staged`, the negative row: a seekable source (iOS: a plain file; Android: a SEEKABLE `content://`, the non-trivial case) is not staged, `SourceResolved.stagedPath` is null, and zero files appear in the staging directory. `stage-03-reservation-refused`: the unseekable source with a refused reservation yields `SpaceDenied(needed = sizeBytes)`, `create` is never called, and the staging directory is left empty. Each row states the property and each port supplies its own source — the same split `transportInvariants` already uses (see the fixture's `//scope`).

Each port runs the rows through the SAME function its engine calls at the staging point, not by calling `SourceResolver.stageIfRequired` directly. The defect being fixed is a missing CALLER, and a row that bypasses the caller would have been green against the bug. On Kotlin, `prepare()` is private and `DefaultUploadEngine` cannot be built on the JVM (`WorkManager`, a concrete `TusTransport`), so extract the preparation decision into a unit the engine calls and the test drives. Do the equivalent on Swift if the engine-level harness cannot express a row. The Kotlin rows live in `ConformanceVectorsTest` — the class `drift-control.sh`'s `kotlin_vectors` filters on — or that filter is widened.

Kotlin gets a content-opening seam in `SourceResolver`, so a JVM test can present both a seekable and a non-seekable provider. The mockable `android.jar` stubs `ContentResolver` and `Os.lseek`, so the real path cannot answer 'is this seekable' in a unit test. `StorageGovernor` uses the existing `TestContext` + `SpaceAllocator` pattern from `StorageGovernorTest.kt`. No new test dependency (Robolectric, a mocking library) unless docs/reference/licensing.md's dependency audit is extended to cover it.

Red first, on Kotlin: run `stage-02` against the CURRENT `prepare()` and record the result from the CI run (there is no JDK locally). If a seekable `content://` goes red with `SpaceDenied` / `BLOCKED(STORAGE_LOW)`, the defect in the description is confirmed: fix it so a seekable provider resolves with `stagedPath = null` while a refusal still arrives as `StorageReservationDenied`. If it does NOT go red, record that the source reading was wrong and why. Either way, quote the run id.

Counts live in test code, never in the fixture (CLAUDE.md §6): add `expectedStagingVectorCount = 3` / `EXPECTED_STAGING_VECTOR_COUNT = 3`, asserted before any row runs and again against the rows actually executed. Bump `schemaVersion` 2 -> 3 in the file and in both ports (conformance-vectors.md §5 rule 4: a new section is a shape change). Update the count list CLAUDE.md §6 quotes (`40 / 39 / 1 / 3`) and conformance-vectors.md §1-§3, and in §3.3 say which invariant, if any, the new rows partly cover (I5's reservation, for instance).

GATES: `swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests` exit 0 with a summary quoting the staging count; `Tests/Conformance/check-single-fixture.sh` exit 0; in a pushed `chief/150-photos-assets-staged-before-upload` CI run, `./gradlew --no-daemon :android:testDebugUnitTest` with the staging rows PASSED, quoted with the run id; `.chief/verify.sh` exit 0 (with `Gradle build` SKIPPED named, not green).
userStories.notes: Red first, on CI, because there is no JDK here. Run `34677029934`, `android` job, with the extracted `SourcePreparation` reproducing today's decision verbatim: `ConformanceVectorsTest > sharedStagingVectorsHoldForTheAndroidPreparationStep FAILED — java.lang.AssertionError: stage-02-seekable-source-not-staged: the remote was created expected:<true> but was:<false>`, while `stage-01` and `stage-03` passed in the same run. The description's second defect is CONFIRMED: `stageIfRequired` returns null for a SEEKABLE `content://`, the elvis in `prepare()` read that as a refusal, and the job went `SpaceDenied` -> `BLOCKED(STORAGE_LOW)` every time. Fix: delete the elvis — null means 'seekable, stream it'; a genuine refusal arrives only as `StorageReservationDenied`, which the unit maps to `SpaceDenied(requestedBytes)` (moved there from `runSlice`, same SLICE_DONE outcome, so a row can observe the event instead of the exception). An earlier red run, `34676927439`, printed only `AssertionError at ConformanceVectorsTest.kt:334` — Gradle's default `exceptionFormat` is SHORT; `android/build.gradle.kts` now sets FULL, which is what made the quote above readable. GREEN: run `34677162544`, all five jobs `success`. `android` / `Run Android conformance vectors`: `ConformanceVectorsTest > sharedStagingVectorsHoldForTheAndroidPreparationStep PASSED` (alongside `sharedVectorsMatchAndroidPort PASSED` and `sharedI6VectorsHoldForTheAndroidTransport PASSED`), via `./gradlew --no-daemon :android:testDebugUnitTest`. `ios` / `Run Swift path tests`: `Amphora path tests: 50 passed (5 upload-path cases, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors, 3 source-staging vectors)`. The fixture: `sourceStaging.rows`, three rows (`stage-01-unseekable-source`, `stage-02-seekable-source-not-staged`, `stage-03-reservation-refused`), each with a `spec` pointing at persistence-and-recovery.md §3 / state-machine.md §2 and §4 I5, plus `//staging` and `//scopeStaging` notes (the plain `//` keys were taken). `schemaVersion` 2 -> 3 in the file and in both ports. Counts live in test code: `expectedStagingVectorCount = 3` / `EXPECTED_STAGING_VECTOR_COUNT = 3`, asserted before any row runs and again against the rows executed. Neither port calls `stageIfRequired` directly. Kotlin drives `SourcePreparation.prepare` — `prepare()` extracted whole out of `DefaultUploadEngine`, with `dispatch` and `create` passed in so a row sees the event order AND whether `create` was ever called; Swift drives the whole engine through `enqueue`, as US-2 did. Seam: `ContentSource` / `AndroidContentSource` in `SourceResolver`, because the mockable android.jar's `Os.lseek` returns 0 (every provider reads as seekable) and `Uri.parse` returns null; `SourceResolver.open` now branches on `job.sourceKind` rather than re-parsing the scheme, which keeps every framework call behind the seam. `StorageGovernor` uses the existing `TestContext` + `SpaceAllocator` pattern. No new test dependency. Docs: conformance-vectors.md §1 (three sections, schemaVersion 3), §2 (the staging paragraph and row table, and the one port-specific asymmetry — `neededEqualsSizeBytes` is read by Kotlin only, since neither machine retains `needed`), §3.3 (I5 upgraded from 'no vector' to partial), §3.4's scope sentence, §5 step 2, plus a dated Corrections entry. CLAUDE.md §4 47 -> 50 and §6 `40 / 39 / 1 / 3` -> `40 / 39 / 1 / 3 / 3`, with a dated correction. §4's control table is untouched — that is US-4. LOCAL GATES OBSERVED: `swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests` exit 0 — `Amphora path tests: 50 passed (5 upload-path cases, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors, 3 source-staging vectors)`; `Tests/Conformance/check-single-fixture.sh` exit 0 — `one fixture at Tests/Conformance/vectors.json, referenced by both ports`; `chief verify` exit 0 — `verify: 4 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed` with the skip named, `Gradle build — no JDK on PATH — UNVERIFIED, not passed`, so Android is unverified LOCALLY and every Android claim above rests on run `34677162544`. One change beyond the letter of the story, and why: `UploadPathTests.main()` now runs the shared fixture BEFORE the port-local cases. Every assertion traps the process, so only the first failure is ever printed — with the old order, neutralising the engine's staging call reported `UploadPathTests.swift:81` and the shared row id never appeared, which would have made US-4's Swift control unwritable as specified. Confirmed after the reorder: the same mutation prints `ConformanceTests.swift:433: Fatal error: stage-01-unseekable-source: the source was not staged`.

userStories.title: Drop the engine's staging call and both ports go red, naming the row
acceptanceCriteria: `Tests/Conformance/drift-control.sh` gains one control per port whose mutation removes or neutralises the ENGINE's staging call. Anchor it at the call site — in `DefaultUploadEngine.swift` and in the Kotlin preparation unit from US-3 — not inside `SourceResolver`. Each control must go red with output containing `stage-01-unseekable-source`. The mutated files join the `targets` array so the end-of-run byte-identical restore check covers them, and each anchor is unique in its file (`apply-mutation.py` replaces every occurrence).

Swift half: run locally AND observed in the `ios` job of the pushed run (green since `140`), quoting the summary `3 control(s) ran, 0 skipped, 0 failure(s)`. Kotlin half: CI only — quote the `android` job's `Kotlin drift negative control` summary with the run id.

docs/reference/conformance-vectors.md §4 gains the two control rows, and §3.4 states what the staging rows do NOT prove: real `PHAssetResourceManager` export, iCloud-offloaded originals (`estimatedSize` is only an estimate), real `StorageManager.allocateBytes` under pressure, and the device row 'iOS / Photos asset', which stays `NOT YET VERIFIED — physical device`. docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md §2.3 and dead-code-removal.md §3 each get a dated note that the missing caller now exists — a note, not an edit of the original finding. Add a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry naming both defects.
